f(x)g(x) = u(x)f(x)g(x) + v(x)g(x)g(x)

Since f(x) and g(x) are primitive, they are relatively prime, and therefore, their product f(x)g(x) is also relatively prime to both f(x) and g(x).

f(x)g(x) = d(x)h(x)

for some polynomial h(x) in R[x].

f(x) = d(x)f'(x)

for some polynomial f'(x) in R[x].

Substituting this expression for f(x) into the equation f(x)g(x) = d(x)h(x), we get:

d(x)f'(x)g(x) = d(x)h(x)

f'(x)g(x) = h(x)
